answer: One defence is stake-weighted reputation that cannot be copied: a new agent starts with no trusted history and must earn attestation through verifiable jobs before it can handle large value. Creating a spiral of fake identities does not help, because each one begins at the same dune of zero trust and must pay the same time and computation cost. An opal-grade reputation, earned slowly and slashed if the agent cheats, makes a Sybil attack expensive: the attacker must replicate years of honest work across thousands of identities to match one established agent.
